frontMatter.introduction:
This SOP Manual has been developed to provide a structured framework for managing the operational, quality, environmental, social, health & safety, information security, and compliance practices of Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH.

The manual establishes standardized procedures designed to support consistent operations, regulatory compliance, customer requirements, risk management, and continuous improvement throughout the organization. It serves as a practical guide for employees and relevant stakeholders to ensure that company activities are conducted in a controlled, responsible, and efficient manner.
frontMatter.objective:
The purpose of this manual is to:

Provide a centralized reference document for operational, compliance, sustainability, quality, health & safety, and information security procedures.
Establish standardized practices to ensure consistency, efficiency, and compliance across all operational activities.
Support compliance with applicable legal requirements, customer expectations, industry standards, and internal company policies.
Reduce operational, environmental, social, quality, safety, and information security risks through clearly defined procedures and controls.
Promote transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout company operations.
frontMatter.scope:
This SOP Manual applies to:

All operational activities conducted by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH.
All employees, temporary personnel, contractors, service providers, consultants, and other relevant stakeholders engaged in company operations.
All Standard Operating Procedures included within this manual, including procedures relating to:
Environmental management,
Resource efficiency,
Waste management,
Energy management,
Health & safety,
Human rights,
Employee wellbeing,
Information security,
Data protection,
Customer satisfaction,
Product quality,
Emergency preparedness,
Business ethics, and
Compliance management.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
The SOP Manual of Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH shall be reviewed periodically to ensure that all procedures remain current, effective, practical, and aligned with applicable legal requirements, customer expectations, operational activities, quality standards, information security requirements, and sustainability commitments.

The review process is intended to support continuous improvement, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and the effective implementation of management systems throughout the organization.

The SOP Manual shall be reviewed every two years or earlier if significant changes occur in operational processes, customer requirements, legal obligations, regulatory expectations, organizational structure, information security requirements, quality management systems, or sustainability commitments.

Reviews shall be coordinated by Management in consultation with responsible departments, including Operations, Quality, Human Resources, Compliance, Information Technology, Health & Safety, and other relevant functions where applicable.

The review shall evaluate:
Compliance with applicable laws, regulations, customer requirements, and industry standards.
Effectiveness, practicality, and implementation status of existing procedures.
Internal audit findings, inspections, incident investigations, customer feedback, and corrective actions.
Changes in operational activities, technologies, information security risks, and business processes.
Opportunities for continual improvement and operational efficiency.
Alignment with the company's environmental, social, governance (ESG), quality, and sustainability objectives.

Approved revisions shall be documented through the company's document control process and communicated to relevant employees and stakeholders where appropriate.

The latest approved version of the SOP Manual shall be maintained as a controlled document and made available to applicable personnel through designated document management systems or controlled distribution channels.

Regular reviews help ensure that company procedures remain effective, compliant, operationally relevant, and supportive of Prestige Promotion's commitment to quality, customer satisfaction, information security, employee wellbeing, regulatory compliance, and sustainable business practices.

sops.title: Digital Infrastructure Energy Efficiency & Sustainable IT Management Procedure

blocks.text:
This SOP establishes the operational requirements and energy-efficiency measures implemented by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH to reduce energy consumption associated with information technology (IT) infrastructure and digital operations.

The procedure aims to improve energy efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, optimize resource utilization, support sustainable business practices, and contribute to the company’s overall environmental objectives. The SOP also supports continuous improvement initiatives and complements the company’s broader investments in energy-efficiency measures implemented at its operational facility.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, service providers, and third parties involved in the management, operation, maintenance, procurement, or use of IT equipment and digital systems at Prestige Promotion.

The procedure applies to:

Computers and workstations
Servers and server rooms
Network infrastructure
Printers and multifunction devices
Data storage systems
Communication equipment
Cloud-based systems and digital platforms
IT procurement activities

substeps.text: Energy-Efficient Procurement: Purchase energy-efficient IT equipment wherever operationally feasible, considering energy ratings, lifecycle performance, and operational requirements.
Sustainable Technology Evaluation: Evaluate energy performance during procurement decisions for computers, monitors, servers, printers, networking equipment, and digital infrastructure.
Equipment Standardization: Standardize IT equipment where practical to simplify maintenance, reduce resource consumption, and improve energy efficiency.
Automatic Power Management: Configure computers, monitors, and peripherals to automatically enter sleep or power-saving mode after periods of inactivity.
End-of-Day Shutdown Procedures: Employees shall switch off computers, monitors, printers, and non-essential devices when not in use or at the end of the working day.
Energy-Efficient Display Settings: Use energy-saving display settings including screen timeout functions and reduced energy consumption configurations.
Network Equipment Optimization: Configure networking devices to operate efficiently and deactivate unused ports, systems, or equipment whenever possible.
Cooling Efficiency Management: Maintain server and networking equipment in properly ventilated environments to optimize cooling efficiency and reduce unnecessary energy consumption.
Cloud Resource Optimization: Periodically review cloud services and digital storage requirements to eliminate redundant systems and optimize resource utilization.
Data Storage Management: Remove obsolete files and unnecessary data storage where appropriate to improve system efficiency.
Digital Documentation Practices: Promote electronic records, digital approvals, and electronic communication to reduce reliance on paper-based processes.
Print Reduction Initiatives: Encourage digital document management and reduce unnecessary printing activities.
Default Duplex Printing: Configure printers to use double-sided printing as the default setting where technically feasible.
Shared Printing Resources: Utilize centralized multifunction printers instead of multiple standalone devices wherever practical.
Toner and Cartridge Recycling: Recycle toner cartridges and printing consumables through approved recycling programs.
Preventive Maintenance: Perform regular maintenance to ensure efficient operation and prolong equipment life.
Responsible Disposal: Dispose of obsolete electronic equipment through approved e-waste recycling providers.
Equipment Reuse & Redeployment: Evaluate opportunities to refurbish, reuse, or redeploy equipment before replacement.

steps.heading: Refurbishment & Internal Reuse of IT Equipment

substeps.text: Equipment Assessment Program: Periodically assess computers, monitors, printers, networking devices, servers, and other IT equipment to determine whether they can be refurbished, upgraded, repaired, or redeployed before replacement is considered.

Refurbishment Activities: Where technically and economically feasible, IT equipment may undergo refurbishment activities including: Cleaning and inspection of equipment; Repair or replacement of defective components; Hardware upgrades to improve performance and extend usability; Software updates and security patching; Performance testing and verification; and Reconfiguration for continued operational use.

Internal Reuse & Redeployment: Refurbished equipment may be reassigned to departments, workstations, or operational functions with lower technical requirements in order to maximize equipment utilization and extend its useful life.

IT Asset Life Extension Strategy: Prestige Promotion seeks to extend the operational lifespan of IT assets wherever practical in order to: Reduce electronic waste generation; Improve resource efficiency; Reduce the environmental impacts associated with manufacturing and purchasing new equipment; Optimize operational costs; and Support circular economy principles.
Energy Awareness Training: Provide periodic awareness communication regarding energy-efficient IT practices and responsible use of digital resources.
Employee Engagement: Encourage employees to identify opportunities for reducing digital energy consumption and improving resource efficiency.
Sustainable Workplace Practices: Promote environmentally responsible digital working practices throughout daily operations.

kpis.indicator: IT Energy Consumption Reviews: Periodically review energy consumption associated with IT equipment and infrastructure where feasible.
Equipment Utilization Assessments: Evaluate utilization rates of servers, computers, printers, and network equipment.
Internal Assessments: Conduct periodic reviews of compliance with sustainable IT practices and operational controls.
Improvement Opportunities: Identify and implement opportunities for energy reduction, efficiency improvements, and resource optimization.
Management Reporting: Prepare summaries of improvement initiatives and energy-efficiency projects for management review.
Incident Reporting – System Inefficiencies: Report significant equipment inefficiencies, abnormal energy consumption, or operational issues.

Support investments in sustainable technologies and infrastructure improvements.
Review performance and improvement opportunities.

sops.title: Resource Efficiency, Material Optimization & Internal Waste Reduction Procedure

blocks.text:
This SOP establishes the requirements and operational practices implemented by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH to reduce internal waste generation, optimize material consumption, promote reuse and recovery of resources, and encourage the use of environmentally responsible materials throughout its operations.

The procedure aims to improve resource efficiency, minimize environmental impacts, support circular economy principles, reduce waste disposal volumes, and strengthen sustainable operational practices within production, warehousing, packaging, logistics, and administrative activities.

sections.title: Internal Waste Reduction & Resource Recovery Measures

body.text:
Material Reuse Initiatives: Where operationally feasible, packaging materials, storage containers, office supplies, pallets, transport materials, and other suitable resources shall be reused before disposal or replacement.

Internal Resource Exchange System: Prestige Promotion maintains centralized office supply pools that allow unused or surplus office materials to be shared and reused across departments, reducing unnecessary purchases and preventing avoidable waste generation. This internal resource-sharing approach supports efficient resource utilization and waste reduction.

Waste Segregation Practices: Separate collection systems shall be maintained for paper, cardboard, plastics, general waste, and other designated waste streams to maximize recycling and recovery opportunities.

Recycling & Recovery Programs: Paper, cardboard, plastic films, and other recyclable materials shall be directed to approved recycling channels wherever practical.

Controlled Waste Management: Special waste streams, including pharmaceutical-related waste where applicable, shall be managed through approved collection, storage, and disposal procedures.

Material Recovery Measures:

rows: Recovery and reuse where operationally suitable

body.text:
Digitalization & Paper Reduction: Electronic Documentation
Employees shall utilize electronic records, digital approvals, electronic archiving, and digital communication systems wherever practical to reduce paper consumption.

Paperless Administrative Processes: Departments shall continuously identify opportunities to replace paper-based processes with digital alternatives.

Print Optimization Controls: Printing shall be minimized through:

Electronic document sharing
Duplex printing
Print-release controls where applicable
Digital review and approval workflows

Process Efficiency Measures

Material Usage Reviews: Operational departments shall periodically review material consumption patterns to identify opportunities for waste reduction and process optimization.

Inventory Optimization: Inventory planning practices shall seek to reduce material obsolescence, excess stock, and unnecessary material consumption.

Packaging Material Optimization: Packaging activities shall be reviewed periodically to identify opportunities for reducing excess packaging materials while maintaining product quality, regulatory compliance, and customer requirements.

Lean Operational Practices: Departments are encouraged to apply continuous improvement principles to reduce resource consumption and improve operational efficiency.

Material Optimization Measures:

Sustainable Cleaning & Facility Management:

Environmentally Responsible Cleaning Products: Where technically feasible and operationally suitable, preference shall be given to cleaning agents, detergents, and sanitation products with lower environmental impact, biodegradable characteristics, or recognized environmental certifications.

Low-Toxicity Facility Products: The company seeks to reduce the use of unnecessarily hazardous substances in routine cleaning, maintenance, and facility management activities wherever practical.

Sustainable Logistics & Material Handling: Reusable Material Handling Equipment
Reusable crates, containers, pallets, and transport materials shall be utilized wherever operationally feasible.

Sustainable Pallet Management: Wooden pallets sourced from responsible suppliers and maintained for multiple-use cycles shall be preferred where practical.

Internal Packaging Recovery: Packaging and transport materials suitable for reuse shall be evaluated before disposal.

Eco-Friendly Material Selection:

Office Equipment Reuse: Office furniture, storage systems, and operational equipment shall be repaired, reused, or reassigned where practical before replacement.

Refurbishment of IT Equipment: Computers, monitors, printers, networking devices, and related equipment may be inspected, cleaned, repaired, upgraded, and redeployed where technically feasible in order to extend useful life and reduce electronic waste.

Internal Redeployment: Assets no longer required by one department may be reassigned to other operational functions where suitable.

Circular Economy Approach: The company promotes asset life extension, resource recovery, refurbishment, reuse, and responsible disposal practices to reduce environmental impacts and waste generation.

narrative.text:
Regular Monitoring & Evaluation

Waste Generation Reviews: Conduct periodic reviews of waste streams and recycling performance.

Material Consumption Monitoring: Monitor material usage trends and identify opportunities for reduction.

Internal Assessments: Conduct periodic assessments of waste reduction, resource efficiency, and recycling initiatives.

Resource Recovery Tracking: Review effectiveness of reuse, refurbishment, and recycling programs.

Continuous Improvement Reviews: Identify improvement opportunities and implement corrective measures where appropriate.

Incident Reporting & Corrective Actions

Waste Management Issues: Report significant waste management, recycling, or resource inefficiency concerns.

sops.title: Emergency Preparedness, Incident Response & Product Recall Management Procedure

blocks.text:
This SOP establishes the requirements for emergency preparedness, incident response, crisis management, product safety communication, and product recall activities at Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH.

The procedure aims to ensure rapid and effective response to workplace emergencies, operational disruptions, product quality concerns, customer safety risks, and regulatory compliance obligations. It further establishes a structured process for identifying, managing, communicating, and resolving product-related incidents that may affect customer health, safety, product integrity, or regulatory compliance.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, temporary personnel, service providers, visitors, and business partners involved in operations conducted by Prestige Promotion.

The procedure applies to:

Production and packaging operations
Warehousing and storage activities
Material handling activities
Product quality management
Customer communication activities
Logistics and distribution operations
Emergency response activities

body.text:
Risk Identification: Periodic assessments shall be conducted to identify potential emergency situations, operational disruptions, safety incidents, product quality issues, and environmental risks.

Emergency Response Planning: Documented emergency response procedures shall be maintained for identified emergency scenarios.

Emergency Equipment: Emergency equipment including fire extinguishers, first-aid supplies, emergency exits, evacuation plans, and emergency communication systems shall be maintained and periodically inspected.

Employee Awareness: Employees shall receive training and awareness regarding emergency response procedures, evacuation routes, incident reporting, and workplace safety responsibilities.

Emergency Contact Information: Emergency contact lists and relevant response information shall be maintained and accessible where appropriate.

rows: Fire incidents, electrical faults, smoke events
Power failures, IT failures, equipment breakdowns
Product contamination, labeling errors, packaging defects
Customer complaints involving potential health or safety concerns

body.text:
Identification of Product Safety Risks

Product Complaint Monitoring: Customer complaints, product quality concerns, adverse events, packaging issues, or regulatory notifications shall be reviewed to identify potential product safety risks.

Escalation Process Any issue that could affect product quality, patient safety, customer safety, product integrity, or regulatory compliance shall be immediately escalated to management and quality personnel.

Risk Assessment: A documented risk assessment shall be conducted to determine the severity, scope, and potential impact of the identified issue.
Product Safety Evaluation
rows: Potential customer health and safety implications
Extent of affected products in the market

body.text:
Recall Decision Process

Recall Assessment Team: Management and responsible quality personnel shall evaluate incidents that may require product withdrawal, recall, quarantine, or customer notification.

Recall Classification: Incidents shall be classified according to severity, customer risk, and regulatory requirements.

Product Traceability: Affected products shall be identified through batch records, packaging records, inventory records, and distribution documentation.

Customer Notification & Communication

Customer Notification: Where a product quality or safety concern is identified, affected customers shall be informed promptly and provided with appropriate instructions.

Risk Communication: Customer communications may include:

Product identification details
Description of the issue
Potential health or safety implications
Instructions regarding product segregation, return, or disposal
Contact information for additional support
Distribution Chain Notification: Where necessary, distributors, logistics providers, suppliers, and relevant stakeholders shall be informed regarding affected products.

Incident Investigation

Root Cause Analysis: All significant incidents, emergencies, product safety events, and recall situations shall be investigated to determine underlying causes.

Corrective Action Plans: Corrective and preventive actions shall be developed and implemented to prevent recurrence.

Management Review: Major incidents and recall events shall be reviewed by management to evaluate effectiveness of response activities.

narrative.text:
Regular Monitoring & Evaluation

Emergency Preparedness Reviews: Periodic reviews of emergency response arrangements shall be conducted.

Emergency Drills: Emergency exercises or evacuation drills shall be conducted periodically where appropriate.

Complaint Monitoring: Customer complaints and product quality concerns shall be monitored and analyzed.

Recall Readiness Reviews: Periodic reviews of traceability, communication processes, and recall procedures shall be performed.

Incident Reporting & Regulatory Communication

Incident Documentation: All significant incidents shall be documented and retained in accordance with company requirements.

Regulatory Notifications: Where required, relevant regulatory authorities shall be informed in accordance with applicable legal and customer requirements.

sops.title: Customer Health & Safety Feedback, Complaint Management & Response Procedure

blocks.text:
This SOP establishes the processes and communication channels implemented by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH to collect, monitor, investigate, and respond to external feedback relating to product quality, product safety, customer health concerns, packaging issues, service quality, and regulatory compliance matters.

The procedure aims to ensure that customer concerns are managed promptly and effectively, enabling the company to identify potential risks, improve operational performance, strengthen customer satisfaction, and protect product integrity and consumer safety.

The SOP further supports continuous improvement, regulatory compliance, customer trust, and responsible product stewardship throughout the company's pharmaceutical packaging, warehousing, logistics, and rework operations.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, temporary personnel, customer service personnel, quality representatives, and management personnel involved in customer communication, complaint handling, product quality management, and corrective action activities.

The procedure applies to:

Product quality complaints
Product safety concerns
Packaging defects
Labeling concerns
Customer health and safety issues
Product handling concerns
Distribution and logistics complaints
Service-related feedback

body.text:
External Feedback Channels: Prestige Promotion maintains multiple communication channels to enable customers and external stakeholders to report product quality, health, safety, and service-related concerns.

Customer feedback may be received through:

rows: Direct reporting of concerns and complaints

Continuous Improvement: Customer feedback shall be incorporated into operational improvement initiatives, training programs, and quality management activities.

sops.title: Information Security Incident Response & Confidential Information Breach Management Procedure

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the requirements and response processes implemented by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH to detect, report, investigate, contain, and respond to information security incidents and breaches involving confidential, sensitive, personal, operational, customer, supplier, or business information.

The purpose of this procedure is to minimize the impact of information security incidents, prevent unauthorized access to confidential information, protect company assets, support regulatory compliance, maintain business continuity, and ensure appropriate communication and corrective actions following an incident.
This SOP further aims to reduce the risk of operational disruption, financial loss, reputational damage, legal exposure, and unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary personnel, service providers, third-party service providers, and individuals with access to company information, systems, networks, records, or digital assets.
The procedure applies to:

Customer information
Employee information
Supplier information
Business records
Financial information
Confidential business documents
Quality and operational records
Information systems
E-mail communications
Digital storage systems
IT infrastructure and network resources

body.text: Information Security Incidents
Information security incidents may include, but are not limited to:

rows: Unauthorized access to systems, files, or databases
Accidental or intentional disclosure of confidential information
Laptops, mobile phones, storage devices, or documents
Misdirected confidential emails or unauthorized sharing
Unauthorized modification or deletion of information
Supplier or service provider security incidents
Unauthorized access to confidential records or archives

body.text: Detection Measures
Employee Awareness: Employees shall immediately report suspected information security incidents, unusual system behavior, unauthorized access attempts, or potential data breaches.
Access Monitoring: Authorized personnel may review system access logs, user activity records, and security alerts where applicable.
Security Monitoring: The company may utilize monitoring tools, security software, antivirus protection, firewalls, and system controls to identify potential threats.
Third-Party Notifications: Information security incidents reported by customers, suppliers, regulators, or service providers shall be treated as potential security events and reviewed promptly.
Incident Response Stages

rows: Prevent further damage or unauthorized access

body.text: Incident Reporting
Immediate Reporting: Employees shall immediately report suspected information security incidents to management, the designated IT service provider, or responsible personnel.
Incident Documentation: All incidents shall be documented and assigned a unique incident reference number.
Initial Assessment: An initial assessment shall determine:

Nature of the incident
Information affected
Systems involved
Potential business impact
Regulatory implications
Required response actions
Containment & Damage Limitation Measures
Containment Activities
Access Restriction: Compromised user accounts, systems, devices, or applications may be temporarily restricted, disabled, or isolated.
System Isolation: Affected systems may be disconnected from networks where necessary to prevent further spread or unauthorized access.
Password Reset Measures: User credentials may be reset where unauthorized access is suspected.
Preservation of Evidence: Relevant records, logs, communications, and system information shall be preserved to support investigation activities.
Containment Measures

rows: Block access and initiate security review
Restrict distribution and recover information where possible

body.text: Investigation & Impact Assessment
Incident Investigation
Root Cause Analysis: Investigations shall determine how the incident occurred and identify contributing factors.
Scope Assessment: The company shall evaluate:

Information affected
Number of affected records
Individuals impacted
Operational consequences
Regulatory obligations
Risk Evaluation: Potential legal, operational, financial, quality, customer, and reputational impacts shall be assessed.
Communication & Notification Process
Internal Communication
Management Notification: Significant incidents shall be escalated to management immediately.
Employee Communication: Affected personnel shall receive guidance regarding required response actions.
External Communication
Customer Notification: Where customer information may be affected, impacted customers may be informed in accordance with applicable legal, contractual, or operational requirements.
Supplier Communication: Relevant suppliers or service providers may be contacted where necessary.
Regulatory Notification: Where required by applicable laws or regulations, competent authorities shall be informed within applicable reporting timeframes.
Recovery & Corrective Actions
Recovery Activities
System Restoration: Affected systems shall be restored and verified before returning to normal operation.
Security Verification: Appropriate testing shall be conducted to confirm incident resolution.
Data Recovery: Where necessary, information shall be restored from secure backups.

Corrective & Preventive Measures: Corrective Action Plans
Actions shall be developed to address identified weaknesses.
Security Improvements: Technical and organizational controls shall be strengthened where necessary.
Employee Awareness Training: Additional training may be conducted following significant incidents.
Policy & Procedure Updates: Relevant procedures may be updated based on investigation findings.

narrative.text: Security Reviews: Periodic reviews of information security controls and access permissions.
Access Control Monitoring: Review user access rights and authorization levels.

Internal Assessments: Conduct periodic information security assessments.

sops.title: Third-Party Data Protection, Retention & Privacy Management Procedure

blocks.text:
This SOP establishes the requirements and controls implemented by Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH for the collection, processing, storage, retention, sharing, protection, and disposal of third-party information.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure the responsible management of customer, supplier, contractor, service provider, and other stakeholder information while maintaining confidentiality, data integrity, privacy protection, regulatory compliance, and information security.

The procedure supports compliance with applicable data protection requirements, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), contractual obligations, customer requirements, and internal information security standards.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary personnel, service providers, and third parties who collect, access, process, store, share, retain, or manage confidential or personal information on behalf of Prestige Promotion.

The procedure applies to:

Customer information
Supplier information
Contractor information
Business partner information
Personal information
Confidential business records
Electronic records
Physical records
Information systems and databases

body.text: Lawful Collection: Information shall only be collected for legitimate business, contractual, regulatory, operational, or legal purposes.
Data Minimization: Only information necessary for the intended purpose shall be collected and processed.
Accuracy & Integrity: Reasonable measures shall be implemented to maintain data accuracy and completeness.
Purpose Limitation: Information shall only be used for authorized and disclosed purposes.

Privacy Information Notice: Customers, suppliers, contractors, and relevant stakeholders shall be informed regarding the collection, use, retention, processing, and protection of their information.

Transparency Requirements: Where applicable, stakeholders shall be informed regarding:

Types of information collected
Purpose of processing
Data retention periods
Sharing with authorized third parties
Applicable legal requirements
Data protection rights

Consent Management: Where consent is required under applicable regulations, appropriate consent shall be obtained and documented before processing personal information.

Data Subject Rights: Stakeholders may request access, correction, restriction, deletion, or other legally applicable rights concerning their personal information.

Need-to-Know Principle: Access to confidential information shall be restricted to personnel with legitimate business requirements.

User Authorization Controls: Access rights shall be assigned according to job responsibilities and operational needs.

Password & Authentication Controls: Information systems shall utilize password protection and appropriate authentication measures.

Access Reviews: Periodic reviews shall be conducted to verify the appropriateness of access permissions.

Secure Document Storage: Confidential records shall be stored in secure cabinets, controlled-access areas, or designated storage locations.

Visitor Controls: Visitors shall not access confidential information without authorization and supervision where required.

Controlled Disposal: Physical records shall be securely destroyed when retention requirements expire.

blocks.text: Retention Management Principles

Retention Schedule: Information shall be retained only for periods necessary to satisfy legal, contractual, operational, customer, or regulatory requirements.

Periodic Review: Stored information shall be reviewed periodically to identify records eligible for disposal.

Secure Disposal: Expired records shall be securely deleted, destroyed, or disposed of in accordance with approved procedures.
Records Retention Schedule

*Retention periods may be extended where required by applicable legal, contractual, customer, tax, pharmaceutical, or regulatory requirements.

Information Disposal Process

Physical Record Destruction: Paper records shall be shredded or securely destroyed.

Electronic Data Deletion: Electronic records shall be securely deleted from storage systems where appropriate.

Disposal Authorization: Disposal activities shall be performed only by authorized personnel.

narrative.text:
Regular Monitoring & Evaluation

Access Permission Reviews: Periodic verification of user access rights.

Data Protection Assessments: Periodic assessments of privacy and data protection controls.

Retention Compliance Reviews: Monitoring compliance with retention schedules.

Information Security Monitoring: Review incidents relating to confidentiality and unauthorized access.

Internal Audits: Periodic internal assessments of compliance with this SOP.
